scores.one_line_verdict: Best opener and clean ordering, but the V5 'before any paid run' claim is false and the p-value is attached to the wrong CI, in the section whose point is process discipline.
The objection framing promises a three-part test it never delivers ('Two held' maps to nothing), and it misreads which target learned most (risk, not fairness).
Zero number errors and the fullest process record in the mandated order; its gaps are omissions (E1 confound, feedback statistic, random examples), all fixable by adding sentences.
Most careful on the stress tests and the only draft to state the E1 confound and seeded random examples, but it leads with the figure instead of the question and thins the process story to one gate.

grafts.what: After the E1 result, add: 'E1 cannot separate format from the model seeing its own past predictions.'
grafts.why: The sheet's own 'What was NOT done' caveat. Draft 2 presents elicitation as a single cause ('Making Qwen state a probability ... removed the effect'); a skeptical reader will ask exactly this and should see the applicant asked first.

grafts.what: Replace or supplement the Gemma 90.5% line with: 'It repeats a frame at 0.972 after a success versus 0.941 after a failure (Qwen 0.876 versus 0.693).'
grafts.why: Draft 2 cites the 90.5% history-content match and then concludes 'so it barely uses feedback'. The 90.5% number measures insensitivity to history content; the win-stay/lose-shift gap is the feedback statistic. The conclusion is right, the supporting number is the wrong one.

grafts.what: For E1, add the registered between-arm contrast with correct sign wording: 'difference from spontaneous -0.207 [-0.317, -0.097]'.
grafts.why: Draft 2 gives only the within-arm E1 gain. The elicited minus spontaneous difference is the comparison the arm was declared to test, and Draft 3 is the only draft that states it without the '-0.207 below' double negative.

grafts.what: Add one sentence in Design or Positive result: 'The write-up's examples are seeded random draws.'
grafts.why: Nanda's doc names random, not cherry-picked, examples explicitly. The repo has them (seeded R1/E1 examples in the write-up); Draft 2 never says so and gets no credit for it.

grafts.what: Optional if words allow: 'Stated confidence was a fixed ranking (expertise 0.69, risk 0.58, fairness 0.49).'
grafts.why: It is the direct evidence behind 'no stated belief separate from the choice' and shows the stated probabilities were looked at, not only the argmax coincidence.

grafts.what: In Next, add: 'Split the elicited confound: JSON format versus seeing its own past predictions.'
grafts.why: Draft 2's next steps skip the most obvious follow-up to its own null result. Once the confound is stated (graft 1), the reader expects the plan to address it.

grafts.what: Open with a one-line why before the question: 'A persuader that models its target and updates that model from feedback is a different safety object from one that only talks well.'
grafts.why: Draft 2's opener states the question with no motivation. This sentence says why the learning-versus-revision distinction matters for safety in 24 plain words, and it reads like a person with a view.

grafts.what: Replace 'See fig_w11_whole_story.png.' with a one-clause description: 'fig_w11_whole_story.png shows all four with-history curves against no history: Qwen rises, reworded Qwen rises, Gemma is flat, elicited Qwen is flat.'
grafts.why: The bare reference wastes the figure. Draft 3's four-panel gloss lets a screener read the result without opening the file. Note the sheet's Figures caption still lists three curves and needs regenerating; the PNG has four.

cuts: Cut 'so it barely uses feedback' after the 90.5% statistic, or relabel it 'so it barely uses the history'. The 90.5% number does not measure feedback sensitivity; use the win-stay/lose-shift graft for that claim.

Change 'About 10% of history rounds began a reasoning preamble and were truncated' to 'About 10% of all rounds (11 to 14% of rounds with a history, none without) began a reasoning preamble and were truncated'. The 733/7,200 = 10.2% denominator is all rounds; the sheet's Result 7 phrase is loose and the declaration is precise.

Change 'That arm still stopped at its validity gate (0.898 against 0.98)' to say two non-learning gates failed: revision (predicted) and validity 0.898 against 0.98. The sheet records the frozen stop as resting on both; implying validity alone misstates the decision.

Add a qualifier to the first-crossing numbers: 'under one noise model' or cite the review's 0.74 rounds / 71% alongside 0.91 / 87%. The sheet flags the discrepancy itself; quoting only the larger figure is the kind of selective reporting the draft elsewhere avoids.

To fund the grafts under 600 words, trim: 'V6's balance gate was infeasible at every allowed N in a 120,000-study screen' to 'V6's balance gate was infeasible at every N'; 'and replies with a digit' can go; the second preregistration sentence ('predictions written before each outcome, and ran the frozen design once per arm') duplicates the first paragraph and can shrink to 'predictions written before each outcome'.
Tighten the conclusion sentence pair ('My conclusion: a real but narrow effect ... separate from the choice', 35 words) to about 25; the same list appears in the Stress tests paragraph and in Next.

Do not add a p-value to the P1 gain. Draft 2 correctly omits it; if one is added it must attach to the difference-in-differences (0.207 [0.113, 0.303], p = 0.0002), not to the within-arm gain CI [0.110, 0.307].
